On tiers with a dedicated accounts origin (`ACCOUNTS_BASE_URL` set), the connector now refuses to serve the browser identity pages on hosts where they cannot work, instead of rendering a page that silently dead-ends. `/login`, `/signup`, and `/manage` answer 421 with a link to the same page on the accounts origin when requested on any other host except the web-chrome origin (which shares the apex session cookie and keeps working); the Google OAuth start additionally refuses on the chrome origin, since its login-CSRF nonce cookie is host-only while Google's callback is registered on the accounts origin. This gives already-shipped desktop clients (which open the login page on the connector host) an immediate, recoverable error instead of a Google round-trip ending in "could not be verified". Tiers without an accounts origin (dev/CI) are unchanged.

The OAuth callback's early-bail branches now emit metrics (`oauth_state_invalid`, `oauth_nonce_mismatch`), and misdirected page hits emit `misdirected_browser_page`, so these previously-invisible failure modes are chartable.
